classes.purpose: Interpret and professionally approve conventions for a specific document type
classes.content: Only professional-selected examples or exact correction notes are snapshotted in the explicitly selected personal/studio workspace. The host model may read full original documents, extracted text, visually inspected pages, proposed conventions, locators and corrections. There is no automatic anonymization or style classifier. Original examples are retained locally until user-directed deletion. Material already read can remain in the same host conversation.

classes.purpose: Draft a new document using approved conventions without importing old case substance
classes.content: The managed drafting run receives a snapshot of the selected approved profile's ID, workspace ID, version, document type, language, scope and convention instructions, without original example files, evidence locators, rationale or owner name. The host sees this snapshot with current-case material through the existing drafting journey, then reviews the final document, current sources and style application. Profile approval is an attested professional decision, not a signature. Code validates records and hashes, not professional correctness. No profile synchronization or central learning is implemented.

security_controls.control: Workspace records bind the exact resolved path and workspace UUID; symlinks are rejected. POSIX workspace permissions must be owner-only. Windows inherits folder ACLs. New-case attachment checks workspace identity and document type/language.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject the operation without activating or attaching a profile.

security_controls.control: Approval binds the exact proposal digest and current revision under a workspace writer lock. Draft snapshots and semantic review records bind the managed Studio Archive context and exact draft bytes. Digests are local integrity checks, not protection against a malicious writer with the same OS account.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject stale approvals, mismatched contexts and post-review edits.
